title: Effectivity of the actual strict scalar quotient tower
statement: Let E and L be finite extensions of Q_l with an embedding E -> L, and let Y be a scheme. For a K-flat complex P of completed O_E-module sheaves with flat terms [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], let N be integralScalarExtension(Q(P)) [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Then N is derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete]. For every n >= 0 its canonical derived reduction modulo pi_L^(n+1) [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] is isomorphic to Q(P tensor (O_L/pi_L^(n+1))), the actual complex integralScalarFiniteComplex before restriction to completed coefficients. There is no completeness, boundedness, constructibility or geometric finiteness hypothesis.

proof.text: Obtain the canonical derived coefficient-system calculus and semilinear scalar-system data for the actual quotient inclusions. The finite balanced association theorem gives the ordinary tensor comparison, normalized on local pure tensors. Apply coefficientExtensionStrictRepresentative_exists to obtain a simultaneous strict model, its finite evaluations, the representative comparison, the actual scalar quotient transitions and normalization of the resulting derived L-sequence N.

Apply coefficientExtensionRepresentativeRoos_exists to the strict model and its transition formula. At P its comparison identifies the total limit of N with the same strict Roos object used by integralScalarExtensionComparison. Composing these comparisons gives a fixed isomorphism from integralScalarExtension(Q(P)) to coefficientSequenceLimit(N).

Apply coefficientSequence_roosModel to the normalized sequence N. It gives a normalized DVR tower T, level isomorphisms to the actual derived evaluations of N, a product witness, and a distinguished Roos triangle on coefficientSequenceLimit(N). Transport only its limit vertex through the preceding isomorphism a: replace its first map p by a.hom followed by p and its third map delta by delta followed by shift(a.inv). The triangle isomorphism has components a, identity, identity, so distinguishedness is preserved.

Apply normalizedDVRTower_effectivity to the transported triangle. Its last clause gives derived completeness of the specified scalar extension, and its first clause makes every canonical finite-reduction counit invertible. Compose that counit isomorphism with the tower level identification, the derived evaluation of the representative model, the exact evaluation/localization factorization, and the strict finite evaluation isomorphism. This identifies integralDerivedReduction with Q(integralScalarFiniteComplex(P,n)) for every n.

proof_origin.description: V8: the same normalized scalar quotient tower argument, using the existing simultaneous coefficient-extension representatives and canonical sequence Roos model as generic tools. The Lean proof transports the actual limit vertex and composes the finite evaluation isomorphisms; no new statement or proof hole.

lean.statement:
theorem integralScalarTower_effectivity
    (P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).FullSubcategory) :
    IsDerivedComplete l L Y D hl
      ((integralScalarExtension l E L ι Y).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj)) ∧
    ∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty
      (((integralDerivedReduction l L Y D hl n).obj
          ((integralScalarExtension l E L ι Y).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj))) ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((integralScalarFiniteComplex l E L ι Y n).obj P.obj))
